sections.h2: Which Ben Hill County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work in Ben Hill County. The Tax Commissioner at 324 East Pine Street in Fitzgerald sends bills and takes payments, and the Board of Tax Assessors decides what the property is worth. Call the commissioner at (229) 426-5144 Monday through Friday, with the counter staffed until half past four, and reach the assessors at (229) 426-5147.

Questions about a payment, a lien or a mailing address belong with the commissioner. Questions about value, a homestead file or an exemption belong with the assessors. The county's assessor page also tells owners that appraisers inspect properties on an ongoing basis, that every parcel with a building permit is visited, and that mobile homes are checked for a current decal.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, receipts, liens, online payments.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: value, returns, exemptions, notices of assessment.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: copies of your warranty deed, kept in the deed room at the courthouse.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Fitzgerald and Ben Hill County?
sections.html:
Ben Hill is a small south Georgia county, and Fitzgerald is its only city as well as its seat. The legislature created it in 1906 out of Irwin and Wilcox land, and of its 254 square miles only about four are water. Neighbors are Wilcox, Telfair, Coffee, Irwin and Turner. The courthouse and the old county jail are both on the National Register of Historic Places.

Fitzgerald High School is the county's high school, and the Ben Hill County School District also runs a preschool, a primary school, an elementary school and a middle school. Headcount slipped from 17,194 at the 2020 census to a 2025 estimate of 17,099. Census figures list a middle home value of $112,700 against a middle household income of $41,758, which frames how much a tax bill matters to an owner here.

sections.h2: When does the Ben Hill County bill come due, and what does lateness cost?
sections.html:
Per the tax office FAQ, December 1 is the usual date for land, houses and business personal property. Georgia's default is December 20 and counties may move it, so trust the day printed on your own statement. One mobile home answer on the same FAQ gives April 1 and another gives May 1, so ask the office which date applies to your mobile home account.

Late accounts accrue interest of 1% a month. A one-time 10% penalty applies once 90 days pass, except that a homesteaded parcel owing under $500 escapes that penalty. A balance older than 90 days can also become a FiFa lien in the Clerk of Superior Court's records, where credit bureaus may see it, and the commissioner is then free to levy on the parcel.

Statements go to the owner, not the lender. With an escrow account, pass the bill along or check that the servicer is paying it.

sections.h2: How can I pay my Ben Hill County property tax?
sections.html:
Cash and checks at the counter cost nothing extra, and a mailed check works as well. Online payment through the county's GovtWindow portal is available through the portal, with PayPal and cards offered only on the website. Each online method adds a convenience charge that appears before you confirm, so you can stop and pay by check instead.

  • In person: 324 East Pine Street, Fitzgerald, Georgia 31750.
  • By phone for questions: (229) 426-5144.
  • Portal help line: (877) 575-7233.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for homestead in Ben Hill County?
sections.html:
Owning and living in the house on January 1 is the test, and the application has to land at the assessors' office ahead of April 1. A filing carries forward each year while you stay put. Move, and you reapply for the new address, while a late filing simply pushes the benefit to the next tax year.

The tax office FAQ notes that homeowners who reach age 62 can apply for an additional exemption. Business inventory can qualify for a freeport exemption where local voters have approved one. For the dollar amount on your own bill, call the assessors, since local legislation can increase the base amounts.

sections.h2: How are values set and challenged in Ben Hill County?
sections.html:
Each winter and early spring, up to the first of April, an owner may file a return naming a value. If the board disagrees it mails a notice with its figure. Taxable value is 40% of market value, and every mill raises one dollar for each $1,000 of that taxable value.

The clock for an appeal is 45 days from the notice date, and the appeal goes to the county Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. Unhappy with that result, you can continue in superior court by delivering written notice to the assessors. Refund requests for tax charged in error have a three-year limit, counted from payment.

sections.h2: What should a Ben Hill County seller sort out on taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Learn the balance and the billed owner before you sign. Because the January 1 owner is on the statement, it can carry your name even when the buyer takes the deed later in the year. Ask the commissioner for a printed balance, and ask whoever runs the closing how that year is shared with the buyer.

A recorded lien must be cleared before clean title can pass. Most sellers settle it out of the sale money, and the commissioner's payoff number is the amount to wire. Needed repairs do not stop a sale while taxes are owed.

faqs.q: When is real estate tax due in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: December 1 is the usual date, according to the Tax Commissioner FAQ, and the date printed on your statement controls. The office at (229) 426-5144 can confirm.

faqs.q: What does a late Ben Hill County payment cost?
faqs.a: Expect 1% interest per month, plus a 10% penalty once 90 days have gone by. Homesteaded property with a liability under $500 skips the penalty.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for homestead exemption in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: File with the Tax Assessor so the paperwork arrives ahead of April 1. Ownership and residence on January 1 are both required.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window in Ben Hill County?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. The appeal goes to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and superior court is the next step.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Ben Hill County taxes without a fee?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash or a check at 324 East Pine Street, or a mailed check, has no fee, while online payments carry a convenience charge.
